title: ConfigWrapper: config_dict is declared-only and must not be mutated; read effective_config
answers: where to add a derived or backwards-compat config setting
how to set a default config key internally without mutating user config
where do config deprecation warnings go
body:
Invariant: `ConfigWrapper.config_dict` in pydantic/_internal/_config.py holds the config exactly as the user declared it. It is exposed as `model_config`/`__pydantic_config__` and merged into subclasses, so never write into it. All consumers read `effective_config`, which both `ConfigWrapper.__getattr__` and `ConfigWrapper.core_config` use.
Derived or backwards-compat settings, and cross-setting checks such as the `validate-by-alias-and-name-false` error, belong in `_build_effective_config`. It runs in `ConfigWrapper.__init__`, so these errors fire at class creation even when `defer_build` is set or annotations are unresolved.
Deprecation warnings for settings (e.g. `schema_generator`) belong in `check_deprecated`. It runs once per config. `core_config` runs once per core-schema build, so a warning there would repeat.
Internal code that needs to inject a default (e.g. pydantic/deprecated/decorator.py:ValidatedFunction.create_model forcing `extra='forbid'`) should get a copy from `prepare_config(config)`, edit that copy, then build `ConfigWrapper(config_dict, check=False)`.
Any new non-ConfigDict attribute on ConfigWrapper must also be excluded in tests/test_config.py:test_config_wrapper_match.
Signature generation (pydantic/_internal/_signature.py:generate_pydantic_signature) no longer takes `validate_by_name`. It reads the effective `validate_by_alias`, so `populate_by_name=True` forces alias parameters in `__signature__`.
applies: any change to pydantic/_internal/_config.py ConfigWrapper or code that reads or edits model config
